claim: GIE extends any gateway supporting Envoy's External Processing Protocol (ext-proc) and the Gateway API into an Inference Gateway; named example implementations are Envoy Gateway, kgateway, and GKE Gateway.
stance_target: the underlying transport/extension mechanism GIE relies on and the set of gateways it currently extends
quoted_support: This is achieved by leveraging Envoy's External Processing Protocol to extend any gateway that supports both ext-proc and Gateway API into an inference gateway. This extension extends popular gateways like Envoy Gateway, kgateway, and GKE Gateway.

claim: InferencePool represents a set of Inference-focused Pods; in practice, adopting it means replacing a Kubernetes Service with an InferencePool.
stance_target: InferencePool selector semantics are Pod-only at the API-design level, positioned as a direct Service substitute
scope_conditions: GIE concepts/api-overview docs page, InferencePool section
quoted_support: InferencePool represents a set of Inference-focused Pods and an extension that will be used to route to them. Within the broader Gateway API resource model, this resource is considered a 'backend'. In practice, that means that you'd replace a Kubernetes Service with an InferencePool.

claim: InferencePoolImport is a cluster-local, controller-managed (not user-authored) representation of an InferencePool imported from a different cluster, populated by a multi-cluster controller, enabling routing to model servers running in a remote cluster.
stance_target: InferencePoolImport is the one documented API-level seam by which InferencePool-adjacent routing can target endpoints outside the local cluster's Pod set -- relevant as a possible integration point/analogy for non-k8s backend support
scope_conditions: GIE concepts/api-overview docs page, InferencePoolImport section, spec at x-v1a1 (alpha, not yet GA)
quoted_support: The `InferencePoolImport` resource is a cluster-local, controller-managed representation of an imported `InferencePool` from another cluster, allowing traffic to be routed to model servers running in a remote cluster. Unlike `InferencePool`, it is not user-authored but populated by the multi-cluster controller.

claim: GIE positions self-hosted model integration with model-as-a-service providers as happening at a higher AI Gateway layer (examples given: LiteLLM, Gloo AI Gateway, Apigee) sitting above the Inference Gateway, rather than within InferencePool itself.
stance_target: InferencePool/GIE itself is meant to directly integrate non-self-hosted/managed model providers
scope_conditions: GIE concepts/api-overview docs page, Background section
quoted_support: This integration makes it easy to expose and control access to your local OpenAI-compatible chat completion endpoints to other workloads on or off cluster, or to integrate your self-hosted models alongside model-as-a-service providers in a higher level AI Gateways like LiteLLM, Gloo AI Gateway, or Apigee.
